title: Credit reconciliation bridge for multi-stage embedding fanout
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a horizontally-scalable reconciliation component (credit reconciliation bridge) that ensures atomic, explainable billing for multi-stage embedding fanout and non-chat tool invocations. The bridge will correlate request provenance across the prefetch/fanout stage, downstream rerank/structured-output executions, and partial failures to emit deterministic usage events and billing adjustments. This aims to eliminate observed overcharging in partial-success scenarios and make refunds deterministic and auditable.
background: We have recurring customer reports where speculative prefetch + rerank + toolchain fanouts resulted in non-deterministic billing: some failed downstream calls were charged, some prefetched tokens were billed even when final path didn't use them, and refunds are handled irregularly by ad-hoc scripts. Existing event shapes lack a stable provenance id to tie multi-stage work together, and the rate limiter reservations are not integrated with the billing ledger, leading to temporary double-counting during quota windows.
goals: Introduce stable provenance headers (provenance_id) propagated across all non-chat endpoints and toolcalls
Create a reconciliation bridge service to emit atomic usage records for multi-stage requests
Integrate reconciliation decisions with the billing ledger to issue refunds/credits deterministically
Extend rate limiter to expose reservation tokens that the billing system can consume to avoid double-counting
Provide dashboards/alerts for reconciliation anomalies and a backfill job for historical corrections
non_goals: Rewriting existing billing ledger; we will emit adjustment primitives consumed by billing pipeline
Handling chat endpoint metering (this ticket is non-chat only)
proposed_solution: 1) Add lightweight provenance_id to request envelope at API gateway and propagate through internal HTTP headers to all downstream components (runtime, kernels, tool runners).
2) Emit provisional usage events at prefetch/fanout time with status=provisional and included reservation_token. Reservations expire or are confirmed by final execution paths.

3) Build reconciliation-bridge service that subscribes to request/response streams (kafka topics: requests, responses, tool-exec, kernel-allocations) and computes final atomic usage events by grouping on provenance_id within a bounded window (configurable, default 30s).

4) When final event is determined, reconciliation-bridge emits one of: confirm(reservation_token, final_usage), refund(reservation_token, amount), or reassign(reservation_token, new_owner) to the billing pipeline via the billing-adjustments topic.
5) Extend rate limiter to return reservation_token with allowance checks; reconcile reservation_tokens with final_event to mark consumed vs refunded so quotas reflect real consumption.

6) Backfill: separate offline reconciler job reads historical request/response logs, groups by provenance heuristics (for pre-2025 provenance rollouts) and emits corrections into billing-adjustments topic for accounting to ingest.

7) Observability: add Grafana dashboards and a SLO for reconciliation-latency and reconciliation-failure-rate; add a canary mode where bridge emits decisions to debug topic before enabling ledger writes.
acceptance_criteria: All non-chat embedding/rerank/toolcall requests carry provenance_id end-to-end (API gateway -> runtime -> tool-runner).
Reconciliation-bridge confirms or refunds >99.9% of provisional reservations within 30s in canary cluster.
Billing pipeline receives atomic usage events and applies adjustments for test accounts in staging; ledger shows zero net overcharge for staged partial failure scenarios.
Rate limiter exposes reservation_token for quota windows and refund flow integrates so quota counters are corrected after refunds.
Backfill job can replay a 7-day historical window in staging producing consistent adjustment payloads without schema errors.
Dashboards: reconciliation-latency, unresolved-reservations, and daily refund volume are live and alerted when abnormal.
tasks: Design: finalize provenance header format and TTL (Ava) - design doc link
Runtime: propagate provenance header and emit provisional usage events (Samir) - PR draft
Rate limiter: support reservation_token API and TTL semantics (Leah) - feature branch
Bridge: implement windowed grouping and decision logic (Samir + backend) - reconcile-service
Billing: wire billing-adjustments topic consumer in pipeline and testing harness (Priya) - billing PR
Backfill: implement replay job with idempotent adjustments (Data Eng) - backfill job
example_event_flow: client -> API gateway (provenance_id=abc123) -> runtime prefetch (emit provisional usage: reservation=rt-1) -> tool-runner fail (emit tool-exec with reservation=rt-1, status=partial_failure) -> reconciliation-bridge groups on abc123 -> emits refund(rt-1, $0.12)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Clock-skew and delayed events could cause bridge to make wrong final decisions. Mitigation: configurable window + Mark-for-late handling where adjustments beyond window are flagged and sent to backfill pipeline.
Risk: Performance overhead from provisional events at high QPS. Mitigation: provisional event is compact (reservation_token + token_count) and bridge horizontally partitions by provenance prefix.
Risk: Billing pipeline consumers may be rate-limited. Mitigation: add dead-letter for adjustments and circuit-breaker with operator alert.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests for provenance propagation and provisional event shapes.
Phase 1 (canary): deploy reconciliation-bridge in canary cluster; emit decisions to debug topic only; use 5 internal test accounts.
Phase 2 (staging): enable ledger writes for staging billing accounts and run backfill for last 7 days.
Phase 3 (gradual prod): enable for 5% of traffic by routing a fraction of embedding/rerank requests with new header; monitor metrics; increase to 100% after 2 weeks of stable ops.
Rollback: bridge has a safe-mode switch to stop emitting ledger writes and mark all provisional reservations as expired (refunds issued by backfill).
